root_cause.summary: screen_training.py passes global split row ids to a collation function that indexes cache positions 0..2351, so the formal Fit loop raises as soon as a batch contains a row id >= 2352, and would pair each input molecule with another molecule's label for in-range ids.

code_paths.screen_training.py:164: cache_rows = [train_rows[int(i)] for i in rows]  # i is a position; train_rows holds global split row ids
code_paths.screen_training.py:165: D.collate(cache, cache_rows)  # collate validates 0 <= row < n_molecules=2352
code_paths.screen_training.py:167: y_fit[[train_row_index[r] for r in cache_rows]]  # label looked up by global id, while the input graph is cache position = global id

root_cause.why_the_cpu_gates_missed_it: G5 smoke and the G4 numerics checks used fit_limit=256 or 128-row batches drawn from the first part of the Fit list, whose global ids are < 2352 (about 0..460). Those runs therefore never hit the range check, and the molecule/label misalignment does not raise. Nothing in the gate set asserted (input molecule id, label row id) pairing over the full 2352-row Fit set.
root_cause.affected_runs: all nine neural runs (A/B/C x s0/s1/s2) use the same loop and would fail identically at epoch 1; no arm-specific behaviour is involved
